payload.because: `blocked` is doing two incompatible jobs, and the render is wrong info: repo-memory-capture 4.1 is a deliberate scope call that shows as `[pending] 0/1` with progress frozen at 90%. Splitting off a terminal outcome fixes the signal while keeping the vocabulary small enough to use without thinking. The three-term render is the honest middle: `done` keeps meaning delivered, the denominator never shrinks silently, and "0 remaining" is the completion signal — with the extra term staying quiet in the common case, which the injected digest's token budget cares about. Name: `skipped` reads temporary and invites revisiting; `abandoned` makes a deliberate call sound like neglect; `dropped` is what people actually say.
payload.chose: Exactly ONE new terminal status named `dropped`, added to both TASK_STATUSES and PHASE_STATUSES. It requires a reason note, and progress renders it as a visible third term — `9 done, 1 dropped, 0 remaining` — only when drops exist, leaving `9/10 tasks done (90%)` untouched otherwise.
payload.over: (a) Adding two or three states (skipped / abandoned / no-longer-needed) — `blocked` already covers "wants to happen, can't yet" and should keep nagging; only the terminal "decided not to happen" is missing, and near-synonyms are a choice an agent gets wrong at 2am. (b) Counting drops as done (10/10) — inflates the numerator and lies about what was built. (c) Silently subtracting drops from the denominator (9/9, 100%) — dropping the hard half of an initiative would quietly read as complete; scope would vanish untraceably. (d) Expressing drops without a new state: deleting the task loses the history of having considered it, and marking it done is dishonest.

taskProgress (projections/templates/shared.ts:101) returns drops as a third term instead of [done, total]. Single chokepoint, 9 call sites. Render `N done, M dropped, K remaining` only when M > 0; leave `N/T tasks done (P%)` byte-identical otherwise — the digest's token budget depends on the common case not growing.

Render dropped in every surface: plan.ts checkbox (line 23) and phase header, status.ts digest + injected block, cli/ui/layout.ts. Agent-facing surfaces stay byte-plain per the CLI output law (cli-ui D1).

Doctor's phase rule becomes `all tasks RESOLVED (done|dropped)` rather than `all tasks done` — otherwise a fully-dropped phase reproduces the exact stale-phase warning this initiative exists to kill.

auto-update: tell the user sofar is out of date, never install unasked

`sofar upgrade` already installed correctly; nothing told you there was
anything to run it for. This adds the telling half.

Read/refresh split: foreground surfaces only READ
~/.local/state/sofar/update.json, and a detached child does the npm view.
No command waits on the network — least of all `sofar statusline`, which
renders on every prompt. The parent claims the slot (stamps checked_at
before spawning) so a per-prompt caller cannot start a herd of children.

Notices land on the statusline (cyan ↑<version>, the info tone — an
available release is information, not a warning) and as a trailing STDERR
line on status/init/doctor. stderr, so stdout stays byte-identical; a
trailing line rather than a doctor axis, so a release can never change
doctor's exit code.

Auto-install is opt-in (`sofar upgrade --auto on`) and pitched only in
runUpgrade's success message, at the moment the chore was just felt.
Installing stays the user's call because an upgrade also leaves repo
wiring stale.

Two bugs the build surfaced:
- The refresh must re-launch dist/cli.js, not the running bundle. The
  statusline executes inside dist/fast.js, which has no top-level entry —
  spawning it would have exited silently and the check would never once
  have run.
- packaging.test.ts installs the tarball into a temp prefix that IS a real
  global-npm layout, so the check fired during `npm test`: a live npm view
  and a write to the developer's own ~/.local/state. Gated on
  CI/VITEST/NODE_ENV=test, and the test now passes the opt-out explicitly.

935 tests green. SPEC gains §Update check; README documents the behaviour
and the SOFAR_NO_UPDATE_CHECK opt-out.
